findings.title: N0N DUMPS DRAFTKINGS AD DATA
findings.comment: N0n posted six-year-old ad identifiers from a sportsbook and called it a hit, stale booty dressed up as fresh plunder for the leak-site crowd.

findings.title: N0N SINKS LIVERAMP, PUBLISHES THE HAUL
findings.comment: 2.2TB of identity-graph data went public because the data-collab company apparently didn't pay up, proof that even the firms selling your identity can't protect their own.

findings.title: QILIN BOARDS UT ARLINGTON
findings.comment: Qilin keeps raiding the academic fleet, this time a Texas university library site, because apparently no treasure's too small when you've already got a thousand other victims logged.

findings.title: SOUL GANG SAILS IN WITH 25 SCALPS
findings.comment: A brand-new crew with no known pedigree posted 25 victims on day one, because the ransomware seas apparently still have room for new pirates with 355 claims logged fleet-wide this month alone.

findings.title: OUTLOOK ZERO-DAY HEADLINES 1,093-CVE PATCH TUESDAY
findings.comment: A thousand CVEs, one Outlook zero-day already leaking NTLMv2 hashes — and credit goes to an LLM, no less. Patch the Outlook bug first, ye idlers, the other thousand can wait for the rum to wear off.

findings.title: CHROME PATCHES EIGHTH ZERO-DAY OF 2026
findings.comment: A use-after-free in the XML parser with an exploit confirmed in the wild, fixed in 157.0.8103.50. Eight zero-days in one year and crews still wait on auto-update like it be a fair wind. Force the relaunch.

findings.title: KQL HUNTING QUERIES FOR THE CHROME UAF
findings.comment: Six KQL queries to flush out stale builds, renderer crashes, XSLT fetches and browser-spawned shells — plus a GPO to kill XSLT outright. No IOCs exist yet, so hunt behavior, not treasure maps, matey.

findings.title: HAYABUSA 4.4.0 "CODE BLUE" RELEASE
findings.comment: The Windows event-log sniper now reads E01 and VHDX images natively — no mounting, no admin rights, no mercy. New pivot-keyword output too. DFIR crews just got a sharper cutlass for free.

findings.title: XALGORIX AI PENTEST AGENTS SHIP DAILY BUILDS
findings.comment: Self-hosted LLM agents that re-exploit every finding to prove it, with v4.6.185 landing Nov 11 and new releases near daily. Every script kiddie's chartering a fleet now — expect yer logs to get crowded, arrr.

findings.title: FRANCE BLAMES IRAN FOR FRIDGE SABOTAGE
findings.comment: Paris points its cutlass at IRGC unit Shahid Kaveh for cooking 700-plus supermarket freezers and torching 15 stores. Aye, the Revolutionary Guards now raid dairy aisles instead of tankers.

findings.title: CEREAL MALWARE SKIMS NATO EMAIL IN ROMANIA
findings.comment: FSB-linked Turla planted new "Cereal" tooling in Romanian and Kazakh Exchange servers, sifting mail for NATO and EU chatter — clever bilge rats using the victim's own server as their crow's nest.

findings.title: CHECK POINT UNEARTHS SPARROW ARMS DEALER
findings.comment: One "digital quartermaster" dubbed CopperDragon arms three China-nexus crews across 21 countries with Sparrow backdoors. Shared malware no longer proves a shared captain — attribution just got harder, mateys.

findings.title: KAZAKH-LINKED CREW LETS AI STEAL TAJIK SECRETS
findings.comment: Silent Lynx told the Hermes AI agent to plunder 2,000-plus national-security docs from Tajikistan, then left its sea chest open for CloudSek to find. Even spies' parrots write the loot reports now.

findings.title: RANSOMWARE GANG CLAIMS VANDERBILT PLUNDER
findings.comment: BYOD crowed it encrypted the university and nicked a million-plus Social Security numbers while students unplugged from campus Wi-Fi. The scallywags bark louder than the evidence, as ever.

findings.title: FAKE COURT NOTICES SAIL INTO LATAM INBOXES
findings.comment: Blind Eagle spammed 3,300 fake court and prosecutor notices across Latin America to smuggle AsyncRAT aboard. Judicial lures for a gang too cheap to write its own malware — respectable laziness.

findings.title: CISA SETS NOV 18 DEADLINE ON COZY BEAR APPLE FLAW
findings.comment: APT29's watering holes, including a poisoned Plerdy SEO script, chained patched Apple bugs into zero-click phone raids; CISA now orders feds to patch by Nov 18. The bears dine on stale iOS, arrr.

findings.title: OUTLOOK ZERO-DAY STEALS NTLM HASHES
findings.comment: Open one crafted message file and Outlook quietly hands over yer NTLMv2 hash—splendid work from the warning system that forgot to warn.

findings.title: BARRACUDA PRE-AUTH CHAIN REACHES ROOT
findings.comment: A crafted config import chains into timezone command injection as root—because apparently the mail gateway needed to double as an unauthenticated shell.

findings.title: SSHOLE ATTACKS DROP C2 AGENTS
findings.comment: Eight attacker IPs were seen exploiting the musl OpenSSH bypass, dropping Python, TAC C2 and persistence; one absurdly long password, and root says welcome aboard.

findings.title: EXPOSED AI PENTEST FLEET SPILLS EXPLOITS
findings.comment: Researchers found 1,465 exposed ARTEX consoles, some leaking implants, credentials and exploit code—autonomous hacking meets autonomous operational security failure.

findings.title: STEALER SELLS PERSISTENT GMAIL ACCESS
findings.comment: Remus now advertises searchable Gmail access after password and session resets for $1,000 monthly; the claim remains unverified, but crimeware loves a premium tier.

findings.title: QNAP NAS ATTACKS SPREAD
findings.comment: More QNAP owners report compromise through the four-bug Plex2Shell chain, with miners and proxyware aboard; patching alone will not evict stowaways already below deck.
